mainTopic: Stories of the urge for idolatry and its capture, worship of פעור and מרקוליס even when meant as an insult, and the משנה and dispute about מולך.
overview: The amud opens by finishing two challenges to the idea that the Jewish people served idols only to permit עריות: a child who dies hugging his idol, and the great cry in the days of נחמיה against the urge for idolatry. Both get the same answer: that happened only after they had become attached to idolatry. The story of the prayer goes on. A note reading 'אמת' falls from heaven, and רבי חנינא learns that ה׳'s seal is truth. The urge for idol worship comes out as a fiery lion cub and is sealed in lead. The urge for sin is also captured, but locking it up stops all reproduction, so they blind it instead. Next come stories about the disgusting worship of פעור, and the rule that doing an idol's normal worship counts even if you mean to insult it, as רב מנשה learns with מרקוליס. Finally a new משנה teaches that one is liable for מולך only if he both hands his child over and passes him through fire. The גמרא then discusses whether מולך is a separate category from ordinary עבודה זרה, with אביי and רבא disagreeing about how two תנאים relate.

steps.title: The captive child hugs his idol until he dies
steps.stepSummary: The story used as a challenge ends: the child refuses to say ה׳'s name, hugs his idol, dies on top of it, and a פסוק is fulfilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The child said: 'Hush, we may not mention ה׳'s name,' a name his parents never taught him. At once he pulled his idol out of his bosom and hugged and kissed it, until his stomach burst. The idol fell to the ground and he fell on top of it, fulfilling the פסוק: 'I will put your carcasses on the carcasses of your idols.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story it brought as a challenge. The story shows a child who truly loved his idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier claim was that the Jewish people served idols only as an excuse to permit עריות. This child shows real love for the idol itself, with no desire for anything forbidden involved. So the story seems to prove that idolatry was loved for its own sake.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'his object of fear/awe', meaning his idol
His bosom, the fold of his garment over his chest

phrases.english: Hush, so as not to mention the name of the Lord,
which his father and his mother had not taught him.
Immediately he took his god out of his bosom,
phrases.notes: יראתו literally means 'his fear.' Here it means the idol he worshipped.

phrases.english: and was hugging it and kissing it,
until his stomach burst

phrases.aramaic: וְנָפְלָה יִרְאָתוֹ לָאָרֶץ, וְנָפַל הוּא עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: and his god fell to the ground, and he fell upon it,
to fulfill what is stated:
"And I will put your carcasses upon the carcasses of your idols."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge story that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the Jewish people served עבודה זרה only to permit עריות in public.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A child who dies hugging his idol shows real love for idolatry itself, not a cover for forbidden relations.

steps.title: That happened only after they became attached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the child's love for the idol came after the people had already become attached to idolatry.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was after they had already become attached to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in just three words. The love for idols in the story came later in history.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the people served idols only as an excuse to permit עריות. Over time they became truly attached to idolatry. The child lived in that later period, so the story does not contradict the original claim.

keyTerms.meaning: That they became attached (stuck) to it

steps.whatToRemember: The starting motive (permitting עריות) and the later reality (true attachment) belong to different stages.

phrases.english: After they had become attached to it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is idol worship. First it was just an excuse, and later they truly clung to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the child's story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the time periods: the early motive and the later attachment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story shows the people always loved idols for their own sake.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story reflects a later stage, after the people had become attached to idolatry.

steps.title: A new source: the loud cry in the days of נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק about a great cry to ה׳ and asks what the people said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And they cried with a loud voice to ה׳ their God.' What did they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second challenge. It quotes a פסוק and asks what that prayer contained, getting ready for the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself proves nothing yet. The challenge will come from the content of the prayer, which shows how strongly the people struggled with the urge for idolatry.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And they cried with a loud voice
to the Lord their God."
What did they say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second challenge to the same claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The content of the prayer cried out in the days of נחמיה.

steps.title: The prayer: 'We want neither it nor its reward'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה (or רב יונתן) says the people cried out against the urge for idolatry, which destroyed the בית המקדש and still 'dances among us.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, and some say רב יונתן, said: 'Woe, woe! This is the urge that destroyed the House, burned the Sanctuary, killed the righteous, and exiled Israel from its land, and it still dances among us. Did You give it to us only so we could earn reward by fighting it? We want neither it nor its reward!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers what the people said. Their prayer shows how powerful the pull toward idolatry was, and this becomes the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the urge for idolatry was so strong that it caused the חורבן and still 'danced' among them, then the people craved idolatry itself. That seems to contradict the claim that they served idols only to permit עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: The House, meaning the בית המקדש
Dances among us, still active among us

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said, and some say Rav Yonatan:
Woe, woe!
This is the one that destroyed the House,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the urge to worship idols, and 'the House' is the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: and burned the Sanctuary,
and killed the righteous,
and exiled Israel from their land,
and it is still dancing among us.
Did You give it to us
only so that we could receive reward through it?
We do not want it,
and we do not want its reward!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹנָתָן: בִּיָּיא, בִּיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3, and this answer is the substance of the second challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They cried out against the urge for idolatry, which caused the חורבן and was still active, and asked to be rid of it even at the cost of losing the reward for resisting it.
steps.confusionAlert: The people are not asking ה׳ to make idols permitted. They are begging ה׳ to remove the urge, giving up the reward they would earn for overcoming it.

steps.title: Same answer: after they became attached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the second challenge the same way: this prayer came after the people had become attached to idolatry.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was after they had already become attached to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same short answer, now for the prayer in the days of נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the time of the second בית המקדש, the people had long been truly attached to idolatry. So their strong urge does not show what their original motive was.
steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges, the child and the prayer, get the same answer: early idolatry was an excuse for עריות, and later idolatry was true attachment.

phrases.english: After they had become attached to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the prayer, repeating the answer of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prayer proves the people craved idolatry for its own sake from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prayer reflects the later period, after attachment had set in.

steps.title: Three days of fasting and a note saying 'אמת'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues the story: the people fasted three days, prayed, and a note reading 'אמת' fell from heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat in a fast for three days and prayed for mercy. A note fell to them from heaven, and written on it was: 'Truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the challenge-and-answer and continues telling the story of the prayer, describing Heaven's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fasting and prayer show how serious the people were about getting rid of the urge. The heavenly note marks a response to their request.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked for mercy, they prayed
A note, a small written slip

phrases.english: They sat three days in fasting,
and asked for mercy.
A note fell to them from heaven
on which was written: "Truth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the story of the prayer from step 4 after the short answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After three days of fasting and prayer, Heaven answered with a note reading 'אמת.'

steps.title: ה׳'s seal is truth
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא learns from the heavenly note reading 'אמת' that ה׳'s seal is truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: We learn from this that the seal of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is 'truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the story for a side lesson. רבי חנינא explains what the note from heaven teaches us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step a note reading 'אמת' fell from heaven. רבי חנינא understands that note as ה׳'s signature or seal. So ה׳'s seal is truth.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it / we can conclude from this

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina says:
Conclude from it
that the seal of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is 'truth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the heavenly note in step 6.

steps.title: The fiery lion cub comes out and is caught
steps.stepSummary: A fiery lion cub comes out of the קדשי הקדשים. The נביא says it is the urge for idol worship. When they grab it, a hair falls out and its cry is heard very far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something like a fiery lion cub came out of the קדשי הקדשים. The נביא told the people: This is the urge for idol worship. As they grabbed it, one of its hairs came out, and its scream was heard for four hundred פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. The people's prayer was answered, and the urge for idol worship came out in a form they could see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The urge for idol worship now has a body: a lion cub made of fire. The people can actually grab it. Losing just one hair makes it scream very loudly, and that sets up the problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The chamber of the Holy of Holies
פרסאות, a unit of long distance

phrases.english: There came out something like a fiery lion cub
from the chamber of the Holy of Holies.
The prophet said to the Jewish people:
This is the urge for idol worship.
As they were catching hold of it,
a hair slipped out from it,
and its cry went out for four hundred parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק כְּגוּרְיָא דְנוּרָא מִבֵּית קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the heavenly note, after רבי חנינא's side comment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The urge for idol worship came out as a fiery lion cub and was caught.

steps.title: How can they get rid of it?
steps.stepSummary: The people ask what to do. They worry that if it keeps screaming, Heaven may have mercy on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What should we do? Maybe Heaven will have mercy on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The people face a problem and ask how to deal with the creature. This sets up the נביא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Its screams are so loud that the people fear Heaven will feel sorry for it. Then they might lose the creature they just caught. So they need a way to get rid of it quietly.

phrases.english: They said: What should we do?
Perhaps Heaven will have mercy on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the loud scream in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to deal with the creature without its cries arousing Heaven's mercy.

steps.title: Trap it in lead
steps.stepSummary: The נביא tells them to put it in a lead pot and cover it with lead, which blocks sound. The idea is supported by a פסוק in זכריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נביא told them: Throw it into a pot of lead and cover it with lead, because lead swallows up sound. As it says: 'And he said: This is wickedness, and he threw it into the measure, and threw the lead stone onto its opening.'
steps.whatsHappening: The נביא answers the people's question and backs up his advice with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was the noise, and lead blocks noise. The פסוק in זכריה describes wickedness being thrown into a container and sealed with lead. The גמרא reads that as this very event.

phrases.english: The prophet said to them:
Throw it into a pot of lead,
and cover it with lead,
because it absorbs its sound.
As it is written:
"And he said: This is wickedness,
and he cast it into the midst of the measure,

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ אֶת הָאֶבֶן הָעוֹפֶרֶת אֶל פִּיהָ״.
phrases.english: and he cast the lead stone onto its opening."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ נָבִיא: שַׁדְיוּהּ בְּדוּדָא דַאֲבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seal it in lead, which absorbs sound, as the פסוק in זכריה describes.

steps.title: Praying about the urge for sin too
steps.stepSummary: Since it is a time of favor, they pray about the urge for sin as well, and it too is handed over to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Since this is a time of favor, let us pray for mercy about the urge for sin. They prayed, and it was handed over into their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: Their first prayer worked, so the people use the moment to pray about a second urge. That prayer works too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting the urge for idol worship showed them that this was a special time when prayers are accepted. So they ask for something new: control over the urge for sin. This opens the next part of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of favor, when prayer is accepted
It was handed over into their hands

steps.whatToRemember: The urge for idol worship was caught and sealed in lead. Because it was an עת רצון, they also prayed about the urge for sin, and it too was given over to them.

phrases.english: They said: Since it is a time of favor,
let us pray for mercy about the urge for sin.
They prayed for mercy,
and it was handed over into their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the success of capturing the urge for idol worship and moves on to a second urge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the עת רצון they prayed, and the urge for sin was handed over to them.

steps.title: Locking up the urge stops life itself
steps.stepSummary: They imprisoned the captured יצר הרע for three days, and then not even a fresh egg could be found for a sick person.
steps.simpleTranslation: They locked it up for three days. People looked for a fresh, one-day-old egg for a sick person and could not find one.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: the יצר הרע captured in the last step is locked away, and the world shows a surprising side effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the urge was gone, creatures stopped reproducing, so even hens stopped laying. The story shows that this urge, harmful as it can be, is also needed to keep the world going. This sets up the problem in the next step.

phrases.english: They imprisoned it for three days.
They looked for a one-day-old egg for a sick person,
and they could not find one.
phrases.notes: The point is that with this urge locked up, nothing was reproducing, not even the hens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the יצר הרע that was handed over in step 11 and shows what happened next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the יצר הרע, the world stops reproducing.

steps.title: What should we do? Half is not an option
steps.stepSummary: The people ask what to do. They think about praying for only half the urge to be removed, but realize Heaven does not grant half.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What should we do? Should we pray for half? Heaven does not give halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The people face a problem: they cannot keep the urge locked up, but they do not want it fully free either. This step sets up the solution in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obvious idea is to pray for a partial cancellation, so the urge stays but is weaker. They turn this down, since gifts from Heaven come whole, not in halves. So they need another way to weaken it.

phrases.english: They said: What should we do?
Should we pray for half?
phrases.notes: He means praying that only half of its power be taken away.

phrases.english: Half, Heaven does not give.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the problem found in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to deal with the יצר הרע when fully removing it destroys the world and praying for half will not work.

steps.title: They blind it, weakening the urge for close relatives
steps.stepSummary: They blind the יצר הרע. This works only partly: people are no longer drawn to their close relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: They blinded its eyes. This helped, so that a person is not drawn to his close relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the answer to the question in step 13: since they cannot pray for half, they weaken the urge by blinding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blinding does not destroy the urge, so the world keeps going. It does cut the urge back in one area: people do not naturally desire their close relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: They blinded (literally, painted out) its eyes

steps.whatToRemember: The יצר הרע was captured but could not be destroyed, since the world needs it. Blinding it only removed the desire for close relatives.

phrases.english: They blinded its eyes.
It worked on it
so that a person is not drawn to his close relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blinding the יצר הרע weakened it partly, removing the desire for close relatives, without destroying the world.

steps.title: The woman who would not serve פעור
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, tells of a sick non-Jewish woman who promised to serve every idol if she recovered. When she reached פעור and heard how it was worshipped, she said she would rather be sick again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A very sick non-Jewish woman vowed that if she recovered she would worship every idol in the world. She recovered and did so. When she reached פעור, she asked the priests how it is worshipped. They said: you eat beets, drink beer, and relieve yourself in front of it. She said: Better for me to get sick again than to worship an idol that way.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins, about how disgusting the worship of פעור was. Even an eager idol worshipper refused it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This woman was ready to serve every idol in the world, yet she drew the line at פעור. The story sets up the next step, where רב יהודה contrasts her with ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: בעל פעור, an idol worshipped in a disgusting way

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
There was an incident with a certain non-Jewish woman
who was very sick.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה: אִם תַּעֲמוֹד הָהִיא אִשָּׁה מֵחוֹלְיָהּ,
phrases.english: She said: If that woman recovers from her illness,
phrases.notes: "That woman" is her polite way of talking about herself.

phrases.aramaic: תֵּלֵךְ וְתַעֲבוֹד לְכׇל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: she will go and worship every idol in the world.
She recovered and worshipped
every idol in the world.
When she reached Peor,
she asked the priests: How is this one worshipped?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהּ: אוֹכְלִין תְּרָדִין וְשׁוֹתִין שֵׁכָר
phrases.english: They told her: One eats beets and drinks beer
and relieves oneself in front of it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה: מוּטָב שֶׁתַּחֲזוֹר הָהִיא אִשָּׁה לְחוֹלְיָהּ
phrases.english: She said: Better that that woman go back to her illness
and not worship an idol in this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּגוֹיָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about idol worship, moving away from the יצר הרע story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The worship of פעור was so disgusting that even a devoted idol worshipper refused it.

steps.title: ישראל clung tightly to פעור but only lightly to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: Unlike that woman, ישראל did attach to בעל פעור, and tightly, like a sealed lid. Their bond with ה׳ is described as loose, like two dates touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: You, the house of ישראל, are not like her. "Those who attached themselves to בעל פעור" means like a tightly sealed lid. "But you who cling to ה׳ your God" means like two dates stuck to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה draws the lesson from the story: ישראל did not hold back from פעור the way the woman did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads two פסוקים side by side. The word נצמדים, used for פעור, suggests a tight seal, like a fastened lid. The word דבקים, used for ה׳, suggests only a light touch, like two dates. It is a sharp criticism.

phrases.english: You, the house of Israel, are not like that:
"Those who attached themselves to Baal Peor"
like a tightly fastened lid,
"But you who cling to ה׳ your God"
like two dates stuck to one another.
phrases.notes: Two dates only touch lightly; they are not sealed together like a lid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the lesson of step 15's story and applies it to ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל's bond with פעור was tight, while their bond with ה׳ was loose.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads the same פסוקים the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the attachment to פעור was loose, like a bracelet on a woman's arm, while the attachment to ה׳ is truly tight.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: "Those who attached themselves to בעל פעור" means like a bracelet on a woman's arm. "But you who cling to ה׳ your God" means truly attached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same two פסוקים but reaches the opposite, positive conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word צמיד is read as a bracelet, which hangs loosely and slides around, so ישראל's tie to פעור was weak. The word דבקים means really stuck. So ישראל's true, strong bond is with ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה reads the פסוקים as criticism: tight to פעור, loose to ה׳. The ברייתא reads them as praise: loose to פעור, truly tight to ה׳.
steps.confusionAlert: The same word צמיד is read two different ways: a tight lid (step 16) and a loose bracelet (step 17). That is the whole difference between the two readings.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
"Those who attached themselves to Baal Peor"
like a bracelet on a woman's arm,
phrases.notes: A bracelet hangs loosely, so the tie to פעור was a weak one.

phrases.english: "But you who cling to ה׳ your God"
truly attached.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the same פסוקים explained in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל's tie to פעור was loose, while their bond with ה׳ is truly tight.

steps.title: סבטא בן אלס tries to insult פעור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a Jew who relieved himself before פעור to disgrace it, but the idol's priests praised him for worshipping it so well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: סבטא בן אלס rented out his donkey to a non-Jewish woman. When she reached פעור, she told him to wait while she went in. When she came out, he asked her to wait for him too. She asked, 'Aren't you Jewish?' He answered, 'What do you care?' He went in, relieved himself in front of the idol, and wiped himself on its nose. The priests praised him and said no one had ever served it this well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a story. A Jew tried to insult the idol פעור, but his act was exactly how פעור is worshipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סבטא meant to show contempt in the worst way he could think of. But פעור is worshipped by relieving oneself before it, so his 'insult' was really its worship. The priests' praise shows the twist: his intent did not change what he actually did.

keyTerms.meaning: Relieved himself (the way פעור is worshipped)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There was an incident with Sabbeta ben Alas,
who rented out his donkey to a certain non-Jewish woman.
When she reached Peor,
she said to him: Wait
until I go in and come out.
After she came out, he said to her:
You too, wait for me
until I go in and come out.
She said to him: Aren't you Jewish?
He said to her: And what do you care?
He went in and relieved himself in front of it,
and wiped himself with its nose.
And the priests were praising him
and saying: Never has there been a person
who served this one in such a way.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּסַבְטָא בֶּן אַלָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of פעור, moving from how people were drawn to it to a story about how it is worshipped.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An act meant to insult פעור was actually its accepted form of worship.

steps.title: Normal worship counts even when meant as an insult
steps.stepSummary: The rule: relieving oneself before בעל פעור, or throwing a stone at מרקוליס, is their worship even if the person means to insult them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who relieves himself before בעל פעור is worshipping it, even if he means to disgrace it. One who throws a stone at מרקוליס is worshipping it, even if he means to stone it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the halachic rule from the story. If you do an idol's usual form of worship, it counts as worship no matter what you intended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words come from the earlier משנה about forms of עבודה זרה. The גמרא adds 'even if he intends to disgrace it.' What counts is the act being the idol's normal worship, not the person's goal.

keyTerms.meaning: Mercury, an idol worshipped by throwing stones at it
To stone it, to pelt it

steps.whatToRemember: An idol's usual form of worship counts as worship even if the person does it to insult the idol.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume a bad intention toward the idol saves you here. With these idols, the act itself is their worship.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that רב מנשה's story will test in the next steps.

phrases.english: One who relieves himself before Ba'al Peor —
this is its worship,
even though he intends to disgrace it.
One who throws a stone at Mercury —
this is its worship,
even though he intends to stone it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפּוֹעֵר עַצְמוֹ לְבַעַל פְּעוֹר הֲרֵי זֶה עֲבוֹדָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story of סבטא into a halachic rule and adds a matching case with מרקוליס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing an idol's normal worship is liable even when the intent is to insult it.

steps.title: רב מנשה throws a stone at an idol
steps.stepSummary: On his way to בי תורתא, רב מנשה is told an idol is there, and he throws a stone at it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשה was going to בי תורתא. People told him an idol stood there. He picked up a stone and threw it at the idol.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story that tests the rule from the last step. This step sets up the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מנשה threw the stone to show contempt for the idol. He did not yet know which idol it was, and that detail becomes the issue in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: רַב מְנַשֶּׁה הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל לְבֵי תוֹרְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Menashe was going to Bei Torta.
They said to him:
There is an idol standing here.
He took a stone and threw it at it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְנַשֶּׁה הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל לְבֵי תוֹרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests the rule about מרקוליס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב מנשה threw a stone at an idol to disgrace it.

steps.title: The people warn him it is מרקוליס
steps.stepSummary: The people tell רב מנשה that the idol is מרקוליס, whose worship is throwing stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It is מרקוליס!
steps.whatsHappening: The people point out a problem: throwing stones is exactly how מרקוליס is worshipped. It sounds like רב מנשה just worshipped it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their short comment is really a challenge based on the rule from step 19. Throwing a stone at מרקוליס is its worship, so his act seems forbidden.

phrases.english: They said to him: It is Mercury.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב מנשה's act from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מנשה's act of throwing a stone at the idol.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Throwing a stone at מרקוליס is its normal worship, so he seems to have worshipped it.

steps.title: רב מנשה defends himself with the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה answers that the משנה only speaks of throwing a stone as worship, and he meant to insult it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: We learned, 'One who throws a stone to מרקוליס.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשה defends what he did. He reads the משנה as talking only about someone who throws a stone in order to worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, 'to מרקוליס' means throwing as an act of worship toward it. Since he threw the stone to disgrace it, he thought he was not liable. The next step shows that the בית מדרש did not accept this reading.

phrases.english: He said to them: We learned, "One who throws a stone to Mercury."
phrases.notes: He reads 'to מרקוליס' as throwing in order to worship it, which he says he did not do.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הַזּוֹרֵק אֶבֶן לְמַרְקוּלִיס תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה narrowly, as being about worship intent only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any stone thrown at מרקוליס counts as worship.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רב מנשה's view, only a stone thrown in order to worship counts, so his insulting throw was not worship. The בית מדרש rejects this reading in step 23.

steps.title: The בית מדרש rejects רב מנשה's reading
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה asks in the בית מדרש, and they tell him the משנה makes one liable even if he meant to stone the idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came and asked in the בית מדרש. They told him: We learned, 'One who throws a stone at מרקוליס,' even if he means to stone it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשה checks his reasoning with the scholars. They reject his narrow reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars say the משנה covers any stone thrown at מרקוליס, whatever the intent. This matches the rule from step 19. His defense in step 22 falls apart.

phrases.english: He came and asked in the study hall.
They said to him:
We learned, "One who throws a stone at Mercury,"
even though he intends to stone it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense given in step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב מנשה's narrow reading of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה makes one liable even when the throw is meant as an insult.

steps.title: Can רב מנשה take the stone back?
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה suggests fixing his mistake by going back and removing the stone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I will go and take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשה tries to undo what he did. This sets up the scholars' final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He hopes that removing the stone will cancel the act of worship. The question now is whether taking a stone off מרקוליס is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: I will go and take it

phrases.english: He said to them: I will go and take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the rejection in step 23 by proposing a fix.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether removing the stone would fix the problem.

steps.title: Taking a stone off מרקוליס is also worship
steps.stepSummary: The scholars answer that removing a stone is also liable, because it makes room for another stone to be thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him: Both one who takes a stone off and one who puts one on is liable. Each stone that is removed leaves room for the next one.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars close the story. Taking the stone back would not help, because that is also a way of serving מרקוליס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a stone clears space for a new stone to be thrown, which keeps the worship going. So taking a stone away counts like adding one. רב מנשה cannot undo his act this way.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes it (the stone) away

steps.whatToRemember: With מרקוליס, both throwing a stone and removing one count as worship. Removing one makes room for the next stone.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Both one who takes it and one who places it is liable,
each and every one
leaves room for its fellow.
phrases.notes: Each stone that is taken away makes space for another stone to be thrown at the idol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מנשה's idea from step 24 and closes the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Removing the stone is also liable.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both placing and removing a stone at מרקוליס are forms of its worship, because each removed stone makes room for another.

steps.title: The משנה: two actions are needed for מולך
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one who gives his child to מולך is liable only if he both hands the child over to מולך and passes him through the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who gives his child to מולך is not liable unless he does two things: he hands the child over to מולך, and he passes the child through the fire. If he did only one of them, he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the rule for the sin of giving one's child to מולך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate actions: handing the child over (מסירה) and passing him through the fire (העברה). The משנה stresses that either one alone is not enough. Only both together make him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A form of idol worship in which a child was passed through fire
One who gives of his offspring (his child)
Passing the child through the fire

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one action is enough. The משנה repeats the rule on purpose: handing over without fire, or fire without handing over, does not make him liable.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who gives of his offspring to מולך
is not liable until he hands him over to מולך
and passes him through the fire.
If he handed him over to מולך but did not pass him through the fire,
or he passed him through the fire but did not hand him over to מולך,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר לַמּוֹלֶךְ וְיַעֲבִיר בָּאֵשׁ.
phrases.english: he is not liable until he hands him over to מולך and passes him through the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story of רב מנשה and מרקוליס ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for מולך requires both handing the child over and passing him through fire.

steps.title: Why is מולך taught separately from idol worship?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that idol worship and מולך are taught as two separate topics.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches the laws of idol worship, and it also teaches the laws of מולך separately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the משניות list עבודה זרה and מולך as two different topics. This is a setup line that prepares the explanation coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מולך were just one more kind of idol worship, why give it its own משנה? The question hides in this observation, and רבי אבין will answer it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It teaches idol worship,
phrases.notes: The laws of idol worship were already taught in an earlier משנה.

phrases.english: and it teaches מולך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the structure of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה treats מולך as a topic separate from עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי אבין: the משנה follows the view that מולך is separate
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין answers that the משנה follows the opinion that מולך is not counted as regular עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said: We learned this משנה according to the one who says that מולך is not idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין explains why the משנה keeps the two topics apart: it follows a specific opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a view that puts מולך in its own separate category instead of treating it as ordinary עבודה זרה. If the משנה follows that view, it makes sense to teach מולך on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said:
We learned it according to the one who says
that מולך is not idol worship,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין: תְּנַן כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the משנה teaches מולך separately.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to one side of a dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מולך is just one more kind of עבודה זרה, so a separate משנה seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the view that treats מולך as its own category.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing the dispute about מולך
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the dispute: the first view makes one liable for passing a child to any idol, while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון limits it to מולך only.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Whether he gives his child to מולך or to any other idol, he is liable. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: If he gives to מולך, he is liable. If he gives to something that is not מולך, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that there really is an opinion that sets מולך apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view treats passing a child through fire as a sin for any idol, so מולך is just an example. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says the punishment applies only to מולך, so מולך is its own special category. רבי אבין says the משנה follows him.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
Both one who gives to מולך
and one who gives to other idols is liable.
Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
To מולך, he is liable;
not to מולך, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֶחָד לַמּוֹלֶךְ וְאֶחָד לִשְׁאָר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion רבי אבין mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an opinion treating מולך as a separate category
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the dispute between the first view and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון

steps.title: אביי: two תנאים hold the same view
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס share the same opinion; רבי אלעזר's view is the one just quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס said the same thing. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view is the one we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds that another תנא agrees with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He first points back to רבי אלעזר's view, setting up the source for רבי חנינא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is linking two opinions. He claims both תנאים limit the punishment to מולך only.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus
said the same thing.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon: that which we just said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא by linking רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון to another תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס share one opinion.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: why the תורה says מולך
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס: the תורה uses the word מולך to include anything people crowned over themselves, even a pebble or a splinter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, as it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says, why did the תורה use the word מולך? To include anything they made king over themselves, even a pebble and even a splinter of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי חנינא's view, which אביי says matches רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא learns from the word מולך, which sounds like מלך (king), that the sin applies to whatever people made king over themselves. אביי reads this to mean that only something treated as a 'king' counts, just like רבי אלעזר who limits it to מולך.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus, as it was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:
For what reason did the תורה use the word 'מולך'?
To include anything that they made king over themselves,
phrases.notes: This is a play on words: מולך sounds like מלך, a king.

phrases.english: even a pebble and even a splinter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the second תנא in אביי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס limits the sin to what is treated as a 'king', like רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא explaining the word מולך

steps.title: רבא: they differ about a temporary מולך
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי and says the two תנאים differ in the case of a temporary מולך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There is a difference between them in the case of a temporary מולך.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's claim that the two תנאים hold exactly the same view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, one is liable only for a permanent מולך. According to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, anything crowned, even a pebble, counts, so even a temporary מולך makes him liable. So they are close, but not identical.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה requires both handing over and passing through fire. רבי אבין says it follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who limits the sin to מולך. אביי says רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס agrees, but רבא says they differ about a temporary מולך.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A temporary מולך is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: רבא means the two תנאים do not fully agree. Their disagreement shows up with a מולך that is only temporary.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מוֹלֶךְ עֲרַאי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's claim that the two תנאים say exactly the same thing.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's claim that the two opinions are identical
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The opinions differ about a temporary מולך: רבי חנינא includes it, while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון does not.
